newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian industry wants share buy back, lower taxes.
newsitem.headline: Indian industry wants share buy back, lower taxes.

text.p: India must reduce corporate and personal taxes, introduce share buy backs and replace a minimum alternate tax (MAT) in its forthcoming federal budget, a leading industry body said on Friday.
India's 1997/98 (April-March) budget is due on February 28.

Senior officials from the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) outlined a "15-point" plan which they said would ensure a seven to eight percent annual growth of the Indian economy.
They said capital markets could be revived if the government announced measures like the removal of double taxation on dividends and permitted loans against shares without limits.

They said the government could widen its tax base and increase revenues if it encouraged non-corporate entities to convert themselves to corporate entities and allowed a one-time disclosure of unaccounted money for investment in select areas. The income from this could be taxed, FICCI said in a statement.
FICCI said the government should withdraw the controversial MAT on company profits. MAT was introduced in the last budget and has been severely criticised by Indian industry.
FICCI suggested an alternative to MAT.

"The introduction of advanced tax provision scheme (APTS), wherein companies be required to pay advance tax as a certain percentage of profits to be adjusted against future liability," the statement said.
